messages.subject: combining position_stack & position_dodge
parts:
Hi, GgploteRs,

I'm trying to create a barchart that has both dodged and stacked components. Here's an example, which gets the picture somewhat right:

library(ggplot2)
my.data <- data.frame(A = c("incr", "incr", "decr", "decr", "incr", "incr", "decr", "decr"),
                      B = c("lots", "some", "some", "lots", "lots", "some", "some", "lots"),
                      C = c("g1", "g1", "g1", "g1", "g2", "g2", "g2", "g2"),
                      value = c(0.1, 0.2, -0.1, -0.2, 0.05, 0.1, -0.05, -0.01))
my.data$BA <- paste(my.data$B, my.data$A)
my.data$AC <- paste(my.data$A, my.data$C)
my.data$BA <- factor(my.data$BA, unique(my.data$BA))
my.data$AC <- factor(my.data$AC, unique(my.data$AC))

gg <- ggplot(my.data, aes(AC, value))
gg <- gg + geom_bar(aes(fill = BA), stat = "identity")
gg <- gg + labs(fill = "")
gg <- gg + scale_x_discrete("", breaks = c(1.5, 3.5),
                            labels = levels(my.data$C))
gg <- gg + scale_y_continuous("", formatter = "percent")
gg

A few of questions:
1. Is there a better way of doing this? Currently I have to create the column AC, which I think is suboptimal. My method produces equal spacing across all 4 levels of AC. Ideally, I would like the child groups of AC ("incr", "decr") to be closer together than the parent groups ("g1", "g2").
2. Is the "breaks" argument in scale_x_discrete ignored, or am I choosing the wrong breaks? I'd like to have only two tick marks for the two levels C rather than the 4 tick marks for the four levels of AC.
3. The positive stacks are ordered from bottom to top (i.e. "lots incr" below "some incr") while the legend has these in reversed order. The colors are correct, just not the order I want. How can I change this?

messages.author: f88374f5413259c6
messages.subject: Re: combining position_stack & position_dodge
parts:
Sundar,

Generally you're going to have to calculate your own offsets when trying to manually specify where you want to place items.  Essentially, you're going to have to artificially make your child groups closer together on the x-axis.  You might find that splitting your AC column into two columns and separating the factors to be useful.  That way you could calculate the x-axis values in such a way as to control the grouping.

aes(x=parentAC+childAC, y=value) #where the value of the main grouping column is 5 or 10 and the secondary grouping is a smaller value like 1 or 2.

So if you wanted the child columns to be closer together, have childAC be the main grouping value.

e.g.
gg <- ggplot(my.data, aes(x=as.numeric(A)*5+as.numeric(C), value))

gg <- gg + geom_bar(aes(fill = BA), stat = "identity")
gg <- gg + labs(fill = "")

gg <- gg + scale_x_discrete( labels = levels(my.data$C))
gg <- gg + scale_y_continuous( formatter = "percent")
gg

Then simply assign breaks and labels as you see fit.
